title: More tests needed into jail death
article: More blood work is needed to determine why a Kamloops man died in police custody on the weekend.
Kevin Paul Mortimer, 33, died Saturday night while in RCMP cells at the downtown detachment.
An autopsy failed to reveal any medical cause of death and the coroner's office hopes the results of toxicology tests, expected within three or four weeks, will explain why the man died.
"It could be a drug overdose or alcohol poisoning, any number of things. We just don't know yet," said Nancy Egely, the regional coroner's office manager.
Mortimer was taking some form of prescription drugs, although it's not known whether the medication played a role in the man's death.
Mortimer was taken to Royal Inland Hospital Saturday afternoon after he collapsed at Aberdeen Mall. Witnesses said he appeared disoriented and under the influence of drugs or alcohol.
He was examined by a doctor and released. Police were called after Mortimer refused to leave RIH and he was taken to the RCMP detachment.
Only hours after being released from hospital, he was found dead in his cell.

Egely said a coroner's inquest -- similar to a trial where a jury hears evidence and makes recommendations -- will be scheduled for later this year. An inquest is mandatory when someone dies while in police custody.
